title: Five Favorites to Win the 2026 MLS Cup—Ranked
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ben SteinerOct 23, 2026Could the 2026 MLS Cup feature a 2025 rematch between Lionel Messi's (left) Inter Miami and Thomas Müller's (right) Vancouver Whitecaps? / Michael Pimentel/ISI Photos/Getty Images (Messi), Elsa/Getty Images (MLS Cup), Elizabeth Ruiz Ruiz/Getty Images (Müller)The 2026 MLS playoffs are officially underway, seeing 14 teams forced through the exit door while the other 16 enter the Round One best-of-three series this weekend.

While some teams have thrived from the first kick of a ball back in February, others have adjusted and improved throughout the lengthy campaign. Now with just a few weeks left to go until the title match, it’s becoming clear which teams are the true contenders, most likely to hoist the MLS Cup come Dec. 18.
Here, Sports Illustrated ranks the five favorites to capture glory.

Cavan Sullivan has the Philadelphia Union in contention for MLS Cup. / Michael Reaves/Getty ImagesThe Philadelphia Union were at the bottom of the MLS table heading into the World Cup break. Interim manager Ryan Richter turned things around in miraculous fashion, leading the team on a 15-game unbeaten rank that ultimately locked down sixth in the Eastern Conference. The Union will battle second seed New England Revolution in the opening round. The core of the project has been the trust in young players. Cavan Sullivan has taken on increased responsibility and ended the regular season with nine goals and 14 assists as a 17-year-old, breaking Alphonso Davies’s 2018 record for the most goal contributions as a teenager in a single season. At the same time, 19-year-old towering center back Neil Pierre has proven to be a key defensive piece, while 20-year-old right back Frankie Westfield has made immense improvements. Beyond the young talent, midfielder Danley Jean Jacques and goalkeeper Andre Blake continue to play key roles in Richter’s setup. Meanwhile, the attacking partnership of Bruno Damiani and Milan Iloski has linked up for 32 goals.The Union have found an approach that works and seems nearly unstoppable these days, peaking perfectly for the postseason. However, with both Miami and Nashville standing in their way, reaching the MLS Cup could be a step too far for the starlets.

Rafael Navarro has elevated St. Louis CITY SC into true MLS Cup contention. / Bill Barrett/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesSt. Louis CITY SC completely rebuilt their core midseason, and it’s worked. Manager Yoann Damet’s men are bona fide MLS Cup contenders entering the playoffs, especially after winning the U.S. Open Cup final midweek, the club’s first-ever trophy. While the team’s recent 19-game undefeated run didn't set the record for the longest MLS regular-season run, it showed how quickly the team has adjusted to a key group highlighted by Carlo Holse and Rafael Navarro, alongside a mainstay between the sticks in Roman Bürki. Navarro has been the biggest difference-maker, though, racking up nine goals and four assists in 12 games after coming over from the Colorado Rapids on a $12 million fee. With the consistency of results and the dominance shown through the recent run, St. Louis have elevated themselves from a sleeper pick ahead of the season to a true challenger, but will have to navigate a competitive Western Conference and avoid any hiccups that would affect their depth.

Lionel Messi's Inter Miami are the defending MLS Cup champions. / ISI Photos via Getty ImagesInter Miami are the defending champions, but haven’t looked like MLS Cup-quality for much of the season, including a spell with just one win in 10 games. Now on their third manager, Kily González, they still struggle to see out games; however, when the team harbors Lionel Messi, then a trophy is still very much in the cards. Messi remains the be-all-end-all factor of Inter Miami’s entire project. He is the favorite to capture a third-straight MLS MVP title after defending his Golden Boot title as well (26 goals). His influence has been unmatched, especially as he grows more comfortable under González.While Messi will determine the team’s fate, 2025 MLS Goalkeeper of the Year Dayne St. Clair has regained his confidence between the sticks in recent weeks. Meanwhile, Germán Berterame has improved—all while Luis Suárez defies reason as a consistent offensive threat with 17 goals in 30 games at nearly 40 years old. Miami won’t have it easy returning to the MLS Cup, likely having to take down Nashville—the team that knocked them out of the Concacaf Champions Cup—but they'd be favored if they reach that point.

Thomas Müller (center) has played alongside Ryan Gauld in 2026, unlike for most of 2025.  / Rich Lam/Getty ImagesThe defining decision of the Vancouver Whitecaps’ season was selling USMNT midfielder Seabtian Berhalter to Middlesbrough for $2 million after his starring performance at the World Cup. In the aftermath of that decision, the 2025 MLS Cup finalists struggled to match the dominance and consistency they showed throughout the first half of the season. Nevertheless, the Whitecaps look back to their best and topped the Western Conference with ease.Brian White has continued to lead the offensive charge with 20 goals in 31 games, despite a dip in recent form. The most significant difference from the Berhalter-led 2025 and early stages of 2026 has been the return of Scottish Designated Player Ryan Gauld. Injured for most of the 2025 season, Gauld had six goals and five assists during the regular season, making significant strides in the second half of the campaign, particularly when Thomas Müller was not fully fit. Even still, Müller had nine goals and eight assists of his own, and manager Jesper Sørensen is ensuring his German star remains healthy through the playoffs. The Whitecaps should be confident in making a run toward another MLS Cup appearance.

Hany Mukhtar (right) and Sam Surridge (left) have been key pieces in Nashville SC's remarkable campaign.  / Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty ImagesNashville SC produced the single greatest season in MLS history, setting an all-time regular season points record (77) to topple the record set by Miami’s 2024 squad (74). While the Herons flamed out in the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs that year, Nashville are better equipped for a lengthy run all the way to the title. The team's core remains the attack, with Hany Mukhtar’s goal-creation ability standing out even more than in his 2022 MLS MVP campaign. At the same time, Sam Surridge has maintained his stellar scoring rate, with 21 goals in 28 games, while enjoying more support than he did in last season’s 25-goal campaign. Add in Cristian Espinoza’s playmaking and Elias Saad’s transition ability, and it’s easy to see why they’ve ranked among the league’s best attacking powers all season. Unlike some past Supporters’ Shield winners, though, Nashville haven’t sacrificed defensive solidity. Through 34 games, they conceded just 25 goals, and Brian Schwake’s impressive goalkeeping has come up clutch when an opponent breaks through the likes of Reid Baker-Whiting and Andy Nájar on the backline. With home advantage through the postseason, it feels like MLS Cup or bust for Nashville, as they look to become the first team since LAFC in 2022 to win both the Shield and MLS Cup in the same year.
